target: Cafodd y bont ei difrodi gan y storm.
english: The bridge was damaged by the storm.
tip: Cafodd plus ei plus a verb-noun is the past passive: Cafodd y bont ei difrodi means the bridge was damaged.

target: Mae'r prosiect yn cael ei ariannu gan Lywodraeth Cymru.
english: The project is funded by the Welsh Government.
tip: gan softens the word after it: Llywodraeth becomes gan Lywodraeth.

target: Cafodd y bont ei hadeiladu yn y bedwaredd ganrif ar bymtheg.
english: The bridge was built in the nineteenth century.
tip: Feminine ei adds h to a word starting with a vowel: adeiladu becomes ei hadeiladu.

target: Mae Dylan yn darllen am newid hinsawdd ar gyfer ei draethawd.
english: Dylan is reading about climate change for his essay.
tip: After masculine ei (his), t softens to d: traethawd becomes ei draethawd.

target: Prynodd Iolo dractor newydd i'r fferm.
english: Iolo bought a new tractor for the farm.
tip: The object of an inflected verb takes the soft mutation: tractor becomes dractor in Prynodd Iolo dractor newydd.

target: Adeiladwyd y castell yn y drydedd ganrif ar ddeg.
english: The castle was built in the thirteenth century.
tip: Ordinals agree with feminine nouns: trydydd (third) becomes drydedd in y drydedd ganrif.

target: Awgrymodd fy ngoruchwyliwr ddull newydd o ymdrin â'r ymchwil.
english: My supervisor suggested a new approach to the research.
tip: After fy (my), g nasal-mutates to ng: goruchwyliwr becomes fy ngoruchwyliwr.

target: Pe bai'r polisi wedi'i weithredu'n gynt, byddai llai o gymunedau wedi dioddef.
english: Had the policy been implemented sooner, fewer communities would have suffered.
tip: Pe bai plus wedi makes a past unreal: Pe bai'r polisi wedi'i weithredu means if the policy had been implemented.

target: Mae ganddi hi gath ddu.
english: She has a black cat.
tip: A feminine singular noun soft-mutates a following adjective: after gath, du becomes ddu.

target: Mae'r stori'n cael ei hadrodd.
english: The story is being told.
tip: Welsh builds the passive with cael ei plus the verb-noun: cael ei hadrodd means it is being told.

target: Heb ei fai, heb ei eni.
english: Without sin, without being born.
tip: The word ei meaning his soft-mutates what follows: after ei, bai becomes fai.

target: Cyrhaeddodd y parsel y bore 'ma.
english: The parcel arrived this morning.
tip: The -odd ending marks the past tense for he, she or it: Cyrhaeddodd means arrived.

target: Mae mis Chwefror yn fyr ond yn llawn gobaith.
english: February is short but full of hope.
tip: Before an adjective the linking yn soft-mutates it: yn fyr comes from byr.

target: Byddwn i wedi dod pe bawn i wedi gwybod.
english: I would have come if I had known.
tip: Pe bawn i sets up an unreal, hypothetical if: pe bawn i wedi gwybod means if I had known.

target: Mae'r gargoyl yn gwylio dros y ddinas o'r to.
english: The gargoyle watches over the city from the roof.
tip: A feminine singular noun soft-mutates after y: dinas becomes y ddinas.

target: Mae'r Gadair am gerdd gaeth.
english: The Chair is for strict verse.
tip: Am soft-mutates the word after it: cerdd becomes gerdd in am gerdd.

target: Mae gobaith am ddyfodol yr iaith.
english: There's hope for the language's future.
tip: Welsh shows possession by placing nouns side by side: dyfodol yr iaith means the language's future.

target: Neidiwch dros y ffens i'r cae nesaf!
english: Jump over the fence into the next field!
tip: The -wch ending gives a command to more than one person, or a polite one: Neidiwch means jump.

target: Enillwyd y wobr gan fyfyriwr o Fangor.
english: The prize was won by a student from Bangor.
tip: The -wyd ending marks an impersonal past passive: Enillwyd means was won.

target: Mae boddhad yn dod ar ôl cwblhau tasg anodd.
english: Satisfaction comes after completing a difficult task.
tip: Ar ôl plus a verb-noun means after doing something: ar ôl cwblhau means after completing.

target: Mae'r adroddiad yn amlygu prif ganfyddiadau'r astudiaeth.
english: The report highlights the study's main findings.
tip: Prif comes before its noun and soft-mutates it: canfyddiadau becomes prif ganfyddiadau.

target: Mae uniondeb academaidd yn hanfodol ym mhob ymchwil.
english: Academic integrity is essential in all research.
tip: Yn meaning in triggers nasal mutation and itself becomes ym: pob turns into ym mhob.

target: Rwy'n cymharu canlyniadau astudiaeth eleni â chanfyddiadau'r llynedd.
english: I'm comparing the results from this year's study with last year's findings.
tip: The word â (with) triggers aspirate mutation: canfyddiadau becomes â chanfyddiadau.

target: Mae'r sgriptiwraig yn addasu'r nofel ar gyfer y sgrin.
english: The scriptwriter adapts the novel for the screen.
tip: The ending -wraig marks a female doer: sgriptiwraig means a woman scriptwriter.

target: Yn yr hen chwedl, mae Culhwch yn cwblhau cyfres o dasgau amhosibl i ennill llaw Olwen.
english: In the old tale, Culhwch completes a series of impossible tasks to win the hand of Olwen.
tip: O (of) soft-mutates the word after it: tasgau becomes o dasgau.

target: Hir yw pob aros.
english: All waiting is long.
tip: Fronting the adjective, Hir yw, adds emphasis, common in proverbs. Neutral order is mae pob aros yn hir, all waiting is long.

target: Bydda i'n bwyta'n iachach.
english: I'll eat more healthily.
tip: Add -ach for the comparative. iach means healthy, so bwyta'n iachach means to eat healthier.

target: Bydda i'n dod â diodydd.
english: I'll bring drinks.
tip: To bring is dod â, literally come with. Here dod â diodydd means bring drinks.

target: Mae beic coch gan Megan.
english: Megan has a red bicycle.
tip: Welsh has no verb to have. Mae beic coch gan Megan is a red bike is with Megan, meaning Megan has one.

target: Mae gen i deulu cariadus.
english: I have a loving family.
tip: After mae gen i, I have, the thing owned soft mutates. teulu becomes deulu in gen i deulu.
